# MatchClaimField { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField(
    raw=None,
    *,
    source_fields=None,
    name=None,
    provenance=None,
)
```

The MatchClaim table: a ``SemanticField[MatchClaim]`` columnar store.

``MatchClaimField`` is the Field paired with the :class:`MatchClaim`
scalar. It holds a large set of MatchClaims (millions of rows) as Arrow
columns instead of one frozen :class:`MatchClaim` per claim; individual
claims are materialised lazily, only when a row is indexed or iterated.
Every kind of MatchClaim is a row like any other: synchronous claims
with their anchors, NOMATCH and conceptual claims without. The event ID
columns are never null: a side without an event holds its sentinel,
:data:`NOMATCH` or :data:`CHUNK`, and its name is null.

Like every paired Field, its struct schema is derived from the scalar by
:func:`~timetoalign.core.fields.derive_arrow_struct` — so a row's type is
exactly ``MatchClaimField.pa_schema``. Its :attr:`table` (and the
Parquet file :meth:`to_parquet` writes, ``match_claims.parquet``) has
one column per top-level property of :class:`MatchClaim`, each nested as
the property is. A provenance shared by every row is held once at field
level (or ``None``) and **injected on read**: the ``provenance`` column
is left null, and :meth:`__getitem__` gives each materialised claim the
field's provenance. Claims whose provenance differs, given to
:meth:`from_claims`, carry it per row.

A MatchClaim is addressed by its id alone: an id held twice is refused,
and an id never changes. A field never holds a row without an id: every
constructor mints the missing ones (``claim_…``), from ``IdMinter(seed)``
when given ``seed=``, from the minter given as ``minter=`` (a loader's),
else from the content minter of the rows (every column but ``id``).
Joining a :class:`~timetoalign.alignment.bundle.AlignmentBundle` mints
nothing.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

| Name       | Type                                                           | Description                                                                                                |
|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| table      | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`)                       | The claims as a :class:`pyarrow.Table` (read-only property), one column per ``MatchClaim`` property.       |
| provenance | [Provenance](`timetoalign.core.provenance.Provenance`) \| None | Shared :class:`~timetoalign.core.provenance.Provenance` (or ``None``) applied to every materialised claim. |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> field = MatchClaimField.from_columns(
...     timeline_a_ids=["A", "A", "B"],
...     timeline_b_ids=["B", "C", "C"],
...     event_a_ids=["a1", "a1", "b1"],
...     event_b_ids=["b0", "c0", "c1"],
...     coordinate_a=[0, 0, 1],
...     coordinate_b=[10.0, 20.0, 21.0],
...     timelines={
...         "A": ("quarters", "fraction"),
...         "B": ("seconds", "float"),
...         "C": ("seconds", "float"),
...     },
...     provenance=Provenance(service="https://example.org/aligner"),
... )
>>> len(field)
3
>>> field[0].timeline_a_id, field[0].timeline_b_id
('A', 'B')
```

### at { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.at }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.at(timeline_id, coordinate)
```

Return claims relevant at ``(timeline_id, coordinate)``.

The selection is a vectorized PyArrow boolean mask over the struct
column. Instant rows compare their start coordinate exactly. Interval
rows use closed containment between their start and end coordinates.
Rows without anchors (NOMATCH, conceptual) are never relevant. No
claim is materialised and the rest of the field is never touched;
the shared provenance carries over.

Coordinate matching is exact in the query coordinate's declared
number representation. There is no tolerance or nearest-value
fallback.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                                | Description                                   | Default    |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|------------|
| timeline_id | [str](`str`)                                        | The timeline the queried coordinate lives on. | _required_ |
| coordinate  | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) | A raw or typed coordinate on that timeline.   | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                                                   |
|--------|---------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | A new :class:`MatchClaimField` holding only the matching rows |
|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | (possibly empty).                                             |

### check_on_timelines { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.check_on_timelines }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.check_on_timelines(timelines)
```

Refuse this field unless every coordinate is on its timeline's axis.

The vectorized form of :meth:`MatchClaim.check_on_timelines`: every
coordinate cell (both coordinates of each anchor, each on its row's
timeline of that side) is compared with the unit and declared number type of the timeline it
is on; the first offending cell is refused with the scalar check's
message.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name      | Type                                                                                                                                       | Description                                                                                                                 | Default    |
|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| timelines | [Iterable](`collections.abc.Iterable`)\[[Any](`typing.Any`)\] \| [Mapping](`collections.abc.Mapping`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | Every timeline the rows name: timelines, or a mapping from a timeline id to a timeline or its ``(unit, number_type)`` pair. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description   |
|--------|---------------------|---------------|
|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | This field.   |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                         |
|--------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If a row names a timeline not given, or a coordinate is not on its timeline's axis. |

Return the claims that involve ``timeline_id`` on either side.

The filter is a vectorized boolean mask over the struct's id
sub-fields; no claim is materialised. The shared provenance carries
over.

| Name        | Type         | Description                                           | Default    |
|-------------|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| timeline_id | [str](`str`) | The exact timeline id to match against either column. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                                                    |
|--------|---------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | A new :class:`MatchClaimField` holding only the matching rows. |

### connects_groups { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.connects_groups }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.connects_groups(group_a_ids, group_b_ids)
```

Whether any synchronous claim spans the two given sets of timeline ids.

True when at least one row with anchors has one side in
``group_a_ids`` and the other side in ``group_b_ids``; a NOMATCH or
conceptual row states no temporal equivalence and connects nothing.
The test is a vectorized mask reduced with :func:`pyarrow.compute.any`;
no claim is materialised, so it answers commensurability over a
million-row field in one pass.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                         | Description                     | Default    |
|-------------|------------------------------|---------------------------------|------------|
| group_a_ids | [set](`set`)\[[str](`str`)\] | Timeline ids on one side.       | _required_ |
| group_b_ids | [set](`set`)\[[str](`str`)\] | Timeline ids on the other side. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type           | Description                               |
|--------|----------------|-------------------------------------------|
|        | [bool](`bool`) | True if some claim connects the two sets. |

### filter { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.filter }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.filter(
    timeline_id=None,
    timeline_ids=None,
    id_pattern=None,
    between=None,
    within=None,
    synchronous_only=False,
    nomatch_only=False,
    believer=None,
    beliefs=DEFAULT_BELIEFS,
    context=None,
)
```

Return a filtered view following the unified filter API.

Every criterion is a vectorized boolean mask over the claim columns;
no claim is materialised and the shared provenance carries over. All
non-default criteria are combined with logical AND.

``include_domains`` / ``include_units`` are deliberately absent: they
need per-timeline metadata (domain, unit) that this store does not
hold. A caller that owns that metadata — an
:class:`~timetoalign.alignment.bundle.AlignmentBundle`, say — resolves
them into the set of timeline ids that pass and hands that set to
``within``.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name             | Type                                                                                   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Default           |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| timeline_id      | [str](`str`) \| None                                                                   | Keep rows involving this exact id on either side (equivalent to :meth:`connecting`).                                                                                                                              | `None`            |
| timeline_ids     | [set](`set`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None                                                   | Keep rows involving **any** id in this set on either side.                                                                                                                                                        | `None`            |
| id_pattern       | [str](`str`) \| None                                                                   | Keep rows involving any id matching this regex (``re.search`` against the field's :attr:`timeline_ids`).                                                                                                          | `None`            |
| between          | [tuple](`tuple`)\[[str](`str`), [str](`str`)\] \| None                                 | Keep rows connecting exactly these two ids (order-independent).                                                                                                                                                   | `None`            |
| within           | [set](`set`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None                                                   | Keep rows whose **both** ids are in this set. This is the primitive behind domain- and unit-restricted queries.                                                                                                   | `None`            |
| synchronous_only | [bool](`bool`)                                                                         | Keep the synchronous rows (those with anchors).                                                                                                                                                                   | `False`           |
| nomatch_only     | [bool](`bool`)                                                                         | Keep the NOMATCH rows (not synchronous, :data:`NOMATCH` on one side).                                                                                                                                             | `False`           |
| believer         | [str](`str`) \| None                                                                   | The actor whose beliefs filter the rows (the belief filter, :func:`~timetoalign.core.provenance.belief_mask`); ``None`` filters nothing.                                                                          | `None`            |
| beliefs          | [Collection](`collections.abc.Collection`)\[[BeliefState](`timetoshare.BeliefState`)\] | The states kept: a row passes when the believer's belief in it (``"true"``, ``"unlikely"``, ``"false"``), or ``"undecided"`` where the believer holds none, is one of them. Default: every state but ``"false"``. | `DEFAULT_BELIEFS` |
| context          | [Mapping](`collections.abc.Mapping`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] \| None      | The JSON-LD context under which the believer and the rows' actors compare as IRIs (a bundle passes its manifest's ``@context``); ``None`` declares no prefix.                                                     | `None`            |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                                                     |
|--------|---------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | A new :class:`MatchClaimField`. With no criteria set, a copy of |
|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | the whole field is returned.                                    |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                     |
|--------|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If ``synchronous_only`` and ``nomatch_only`` are both set, or ``beliefs`` is not a collection of belief states. |

### from_claims { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.from_claims }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.from_claims(claims, *, provenance=None)
```

Build a field from existing :class:`MatchClaim` objects.

Every kind of claim is a row: synchronous claims with their anchors
(interval claims with both), NOMATCH and conceptual claims without.
Each row keeps every property of its claim, so every claim
materialises equal to the one stored. A MatchClaim is addressed by
its id alone: two claims under one id are refused (an id is never
renamed); every claim holds its id from construction.

If ``provenance`` is ``None`` and all claims share one equal
:class:`~timetoalign.core.provenance.Provenance`, it is adopted as
the field-level provenance and the rows carry none. If the claims'
provenance differs (``None`` included), the field's stays ``None``
and each row carries its own claim's.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name       | Type                                                                                              | Description                                                                   | Default    |
|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| claims     | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[MatchClaim](`timetoalign.alignment.claims.MatchClaim`)\] | The claims to store.                                                          | _required_ |
| provenance | [Provenance](`timetoalign.core.provenance.Provenance`) \| None                                    | Explicit field-level provenance. When provided it replaces every claim's own. | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                     |
|--------|---------------------|---------------------------------|
|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | A new :class:`MatchClaimField`. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If two claims hold the same id, or an anchor holds a coordinate no cell can hold (a non-finite number), which every reader of the MatchClaim table refuses. |

### from_columns { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.from_columns }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.from_columns(
    timeline_a_ids,
    timeline_b_ids,
    event_a_ids,
    event_b_ids,
    coordinate_a,
    coordinate_b,
    *,
    timelines,
    end_coordinate_a=None,
    end_coordinate_b=None,
    certainty=1.0,
    provenance=None,
    seed=None,
    minter=None,
)
```

Build a field of event matches from parallel columns (the vectorized path).

This is the constructor a bulk producer (e.g. an alignment loader)
uses. It assembles the derived ``MatchClaim`` struct array straight
from the parallel inputs and **never** materialises a single
:class:`MatchClaim` Python object, so it scales to millions of rows.

Each row is a synchronous claim between two sides: the timeline
and event ids are filled from the inputs, a side an event ID or
:data:`CHUNK` (a position on a timeline holding no event for it),
and every coordinate is a position on its row's timeline, written in that timeline's unit and
declared number type. With the two end columns, every row with an
end on both sides is an interval claim. The ids are minted, in row
order (:class:`MatchClaimField`). Names are left null,
and so is the ``provenance`` column (the shared provenance is
injected on read). The field is checked against the timelines
(:meth:`check_on_timelines`).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name             | Type                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Description                                                                                                                 | Default    |
|------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| timeline_a_ids   | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[Array](`pyarrow.Array`) \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[ChunkedArray](`pyarrow.ChunkedArray`)                                                                         | Timeline-A ids, one per claim.                                                                                              | _required_ |
| timeline_b_ids   | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[Array](`pyarrow.Array`) \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[ChunkedArray](`pyarrow.ChunkedArray`)                                                                         | Timeline-B ids, one per claim.                                                                                              | _required_ |
| event_a_ids      | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[Array](`pyarrow.Array`) \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[ChunkedArray](`pyarrow.ChunkedArray`)                                                                         | The event on timeline A, or :data:`CHUNK`, one per claim.                                                                   | _required_ |
| event_b_ids      | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[Array](`pyarrow.Array`) \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[ChunkedArray](`pyarrow.ChunkedArray`)                                                                         | The event on timeline B, or :data:`CHUNK`, one per claim.                                                                   | _required_ |
| coordinate_a     | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[int](`int`) \| [float](`float`) \| [Fraction](`fractions.Fraction`)\] \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[Array](`pyarrow.Array`) \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[ChunkedArray](`pyarrow.ChunkedArray`)                 | The position of side A on timeline A.                                                                                       | _required_ |
| coordinate_b     | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[int](`int`) \| [float](`float`) \| [Fraction](`fractions.Fraction`)\] \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[Array](`pyarrow.Array`) \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[ChunkedArray](`pyarrow.ChunkedArray`)                 | The position of side B on timeline B.                                                                                       | _required_ |
| timelines        | [Iterable](`collections.abc.Iterable`)\[[Any](`typing.Any`)\] \| [Mapping](`collections.abc.Mapping`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\]                                                                                           | Every timeline the rows name: timelines, or a mapping from a timeline id to a timeline or its ``(unit, number_type)`` pair. | _required_ |
| end_coordinate_a | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[int](`int`) \| [float](`float`) \| [Fraction](`fractions.Fraction`) \| None\] \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[Array](`pyarrow.Array`) \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[ChunkedArray](`pyarrow.ChunkedArray`) \| None | The end of each event on timeline A (null on both sides for an instant claim).                                              | `None`     |
| end_coordinate_b | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[int](`int`) \| [float](`float`) \| [Fraction](`fractions.Fraction`) \| None\] \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[Array](`pyarrow.Array`) \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[ChunkedArray](`pyarrow.ChunkedArray`) \| None | The end of each event on timeline B.                                                                                        | `None`     |
| certainty        | [float](`float`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | How certain every claim is, in [0, 1].                                                                                      | `1.0`      |
| provenance       | [Provenance](`timetoalign.core.provenance.Provenance`) \| None                                                                                                                                                                       | Shared provenance for every claim in the field.                                                                             | `None`     |
| seed             | [int](`int`) \| None                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | The seed of the minter of the ids.                                                                                          | `None`     |
| minter           | [IdMinter](`timetoalign.core.ids.IdMinter`) \| None                                                                                                                                                                                  | The minter of the ids (a loader's).                                                                                         | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                     |
|--------|---------------------|---------------------------------|
|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | A new :class:`MatchClaimField`. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|--------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [TypeError](`TypeError`)   | If both *seed* and *minter* are given.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If the inputs do not all have the same length, a row names no event ID or sentinel on a side (a null), names :data:`NOMATCH` (a synchronous claim names an event or :data:`CHUNK`), a row names a timeline not among *timelines*, the end columns are given one without the other, a row gives an end on one side only, or a coordinate is a number no cell holds (a NaN). |

### from_dict { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.from_dict }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.from_dict(data, *, seed=None, minter=None)
```

Deserialize a field from a plain dictionary (inverse of :meth:`to_dict`).

The mapping holds ``provenance`` (the field's
:meth:`~timetoalign.core.provenance.Provenance.to_dict`, or ``None``)
and ``rows``: one mapping per claim whose keys are the
:attr:`table`'s columns. Each coordinate is a coordinate dict
(``{unit, number_type, value}``), read by
:func:`~timetoalign.core.retrieval.coordinate_from_dict` and written
into its storage cell as :meth:`from_claims` writes a claim's; every
other cell is read as stored. A field built from claims therefore
comes back with an equal table and equal claims. A row without an id
is minted one (:class:`MatchClaimField`).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description                                 | Default    |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|------------|
| data   | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | A mapping as :meth:`to_dict` writes it.     | _required_ |
| seed   | [int](`int`) \| None                                | The seed of the minter of the missing ids.  | `None`     |
| minter | [IdMinter](`timetoalign.core.ids.IdMinter`) \| None | The minter of the missing ids (a loader's). | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                     |
|--------|---------------------|---------------------------------|
|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | A new :class:`MatchClaimField`. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|--------|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [TypeError](`TypeError`)   | If both *seed* and *minter* are given.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If a mapping, at any depth, lacks a key it must hold or holds an unknown one (the mapping itself, row, anchor, provenance, belief, coordinate), or a coordinate dict is invalid; if a row is not a MatchClaim (:meth:`_read`); if the mapping carries provenance both under its key ``provenance`` and in its rows; or if two rows hold the same id. |

### from_package_table { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.from_package_table }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.from_package_table(table, *, seed=None, minter=None)
```

Read a field from a MatchClaim table in the package form.

The inverse of :attr:`package_table`: every anchor coordinate cell is
read back from the package form, then the table is read as
:meth:`from_table` reads one. A cell whose numbers do not stand as
its ``number_type`` says (an int ``(n, null, null)``, a fraction
``(n, d >= 1, null)``, a float ``(null, null, x)``) is refused.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description                                                                                      | Default    |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| table  | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`)            | A table as :attr:`package_table` gives it, or as read from a package's ``match_claims.parquet``. | _required_ |
| seed   | [int](`int`) \| None                                | The seed of the minter of the missing ids.                                                       | `None`     |
| minter | [IdMinter](`timetoalign.core.ids.IdMinter`) \| None | The minter of the missing ids (a loader's).                                                      | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                     |
|--------|---------------------|---------------------------------|
|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | A new :class:`MatchClaimField`. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                            |
|--------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [TypeError](`TypeError`)   | If both *seed* and *minter* are given.                                                 |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | As :meth:`from_table`, or naming the column and row of a cell not in the package form. |

### from_parquet { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.from_parquet }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.from_parquet(
```

Read the MatchClaim table from its Parquet file.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name      | Type                                                                                                                                               | Description                                                                                                             | Default    |
|-----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| path      | [str](`str`) \| [os](`os`).[PathLike](`os.PathLike`)\[[str](`str`)\]                                                                               | The file, or a directory holding :attr:`file_name` (``match_claims.parquet``).                                          | _required_ |
| timelines | [Iterable](`collections.abc.Iterable`)\[[Any](`typing.Any`)\] \| [Mapping](`collections.abc.Mapping`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] \| None | Where given, the timelines the rows name (as :meth:`check_on_timelines` takes them); the field is checked against them. | `None`     |
| seed      | [int](`int`) \| None                                                                                                                               | The seed of the minter of the missing ids.                                                                              | `None`     |
| minter    | [IdMinter](`timetoalign.core.ids.IdMinter`) \| None                                                                                                | The minter of the missing ids (a loader's).                                                                             | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                                          |
|--------|---------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | The field :meth:`to_parquet` wrote, value for value. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                              |
|--------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [TypeError](`TypeError`)   | If both *seed* and *minter* are given.                   |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | As :meth:`from_table`, or as :meth:`check_on_timelines`. |

### from_table { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.from_table }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.from_table(table, *, seed=None, minter=None)
```

Read a field back from its Arrow table (inverse of :attr:`table`).

The table must hold one column per top-level property of
:class:`MatchClaim`, named and typed as the fields of
:attr:`pa_schema`; the columns are read by name, in any order, and
may be chunked, as they are when the table was read from Parquet.
Further columns (any other name, such as a ``scope`` column a
package written by an earlier tool holds) are kept as they stand,
after the properties, and never read: :attr:`table` and the file
:meth:`to_parquet` writes hold them again, and the field's own
queries carry them row for row. The field-level provenance travels
in the table's schema metadata under TimeToShare's key
``timetoshare:provenance`` (the JSON of
:meth:`~timetoalign.core.provenance.Provenance.to_dict`); a table
without that key gives a field whose provenance is ``None``. Every
row is kept as stored; a row without an id is minted one
(:class:`MatchClaimField`).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description                                 | Default    |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|------------|
| table  | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`)            | A table as written by :attr:`table`.        | _required_ |
| seed   | [int](`int`) \| None                                | The seed of the minter of the missing ids.  | `None`     |
| minter | [IdMinter](`timetoalign.core.ids.IdMinter`) \| None | The minter of the missing ids (a loader's). | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                     |
|--------|---------------------|---------------------------------|
|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | A new :class:`MatchClaimField`. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [TypeError](`TypeError`)   | If both *seed* and *minter* are given.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If the table lacks a column of a ``MatchClaim`` property, or a column's type is not the property's; if a row is not a MatchClaim (:meth:`_read`); if the table carries provenance both in its schema metadata and in its rows; or if two rows hold the same id (a MatchClaim is addressed by its id alone). |

### to_claims { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.to_claims }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.to_claims()
```

Materialise every row into a list of :class:`MatchClaim` objects.

This is ``O(n)`` and defeats the columnar purpose for large sets; it
is provided for convenience and round-tripping, not for hot paths.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                      | Description                    |
|--------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[[MatchClaim](`timetoalign.alignment.claims.MatchClaim`)\] | A list of claims, one per row. |

### to_dict { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.to_dict }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.to_dict()
```

Render the :attr:`table` as a plain dictionary (inverse of :meth:`from_dict`).

``{"provenance": ..., "rows": [...]}``: the field's provenance
(:meth:`~timetoalign.core.provenance.Provenance.to_dict`, or
``None``) and one mapping per claim whose keys are the table's
columns. A coordinate cell is written as a coordinate dict
(:func:`~timetoalign.core.retrieval.coordinate_to_dict`: ``unit``,
``number_type``, ``value``, a Fraction as ``[numerator,
denominator]``), the value the materialised claim holds, as
:meth:`MatchClaim.to_dict` writes it; every other cell as stored, a
nested property a nested mapping. Every value is a string, number,
boolean, ``None``, mapping or list, so the dictionary can be written
as JSON or YAML.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description                |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
|        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | A round-trippable mapping. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> field = MatchClaimField.from_columns(
...     ["score"], ["audio"], ["n1"], ["o1"], [Fraction(1, 3)], [0.5],
...     timelines={
...         "score": ("quarters", "fraction"),
...         "audio": ("seconds", "float"),
...     },
...     seed=0,
... )
>>> row = field.to_dict()["rows"][0]
>>> row["start_anchor"]["coordinate_a"]
{'unit': 'quarters', 'number_type': 'fraction', 'value': [1, 3]}
>>> row["start_anchor"]["coordinate_b"]
{'unit': 'seconds', 'number_type': 'float', 'value': 0.5}
>>> row["id"], row["end_anchor"]
('claim_1be6k8ij6dzad', None)
```

### to_parquet { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.to_parquet }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.to_parquet(path)
```

Write the MatchClaim table to its Parquet file.

The file holds :attr:`package_table` (each anchor coordinate's
number written once, by its number type), the field-level
provenance in its schema metadata, so :meth:`from_parquet` reads
back every value exactly; further columns of a table read follow
the properties (:meth:`from_table`). Where the file exists, the new
table must succeed it: every MatchClaim of the existing table, by
its id, is in this one, with the same timelines, events, anchors and
every other value; only its provenance may differ (a MatchClaim is
never removed and never changed, only believed or disbelieved). The
file is replaced whole, never in part: a write that fails leaves the
file as it was and no temporary file.

Every MatchClaim written holds an id, which a named MatchStamp may
record: a field holds an id in every row from its construction.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                                                 | Description                                                                    | Default    |
|--------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| path   | [str](`str`) \| [os](`os`).[PathLike](`os.PathLike`)\[[str](`str`)\] | The file, or a directory to hold :attr:`file_name` (``match_claims.parquet``). | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                   | Description                   |
|--------|------------------------|-------------------------------|
|        | [Path](`pathlib.Path`) | The path of the file written. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                               |
|--------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If a row holds no id, or the existing table holds a MatchClaim this one lacks or changes. |

### with_belief { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.with_belief }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.with_belief(claim_id, belief, *, context=None)
```

A copy of the table whose MatchClaim *claim_id* holds *belief*.

Only that row's provenance changes, as :meth:`MatchClaim.with_belief`
changes a claim's; every other row, and every other column, is kept.
A provenance the field holds once for every row stays shared where
the field has one row; otherwise every row then carries its own,
since one row's differs.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name     | Type                                                                              | Description                                                                          | Default    |
|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| claim_id | [str](`str`)                                                                      | The MatchClaim's id, held by one row.                                                | _required_ |
| belief   | [Belief](`timetoalign.core.provenance.Belief`)                                    | The belief.                                                                          | _required_ |
| context  | [Mapping](`collections.abc.Mapping`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] \| None | The JSON-LD context under which actors compare as IRIs; ``None`` declares no prefix. | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                               |
|--------|---------------------|-------------------------------------------|
|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | The new field; this one is left as it is. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                   | Description                 |
|--------|------------------------|-----------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`) | If no row holds *claim_id*. |
